lesson: Today we work on one technique, withholding. That means the poem leaves something out on purpose and never explains it. Look at the list. You've got a list somewhere, pencil-thinness thread, the small accounts that want their columns squared. The poem never tells you what is on the list. It never says what the work is or why you owe it. It calls it the day's real work and stops there. This works in a plain way because the poem does not name the tasks. You fill them in with your own. The gap makes you supply your own warning, your own chores, your own debts. That pulls you in faster than a full list would. Try this. Write about a task, but cut the part that says what the task is. Leave the feeling and remove the facts. The second time through, hold on to everything the poem never tells you and let so up push you before you know where. Here is the poem.
